chunks: Among people, there are some whose child's lineage is concealed out of fear that their family will kill him, greedy for his inheritance.
Customs have proceeded in this manner, so it is not fitting to be astonished by something like it in the Master of the Age (peace be upon him).
We have witnessed much of this kind and heard not a little of it, so we will not prolong mentioning it because it is known through customs.

And how many we have found whose lineage was established after their father's death after a long period, and no one knew it, until two Muslim men testified to his lineage; and the father had made them witness to himself in secrecy from his family and out of fear of his wife and his family, so he bequeathed it to them, and they testified after his death, or they testified to his contract with a woman in a valid contract, and she bore a child who could be from him, so it became obligatory by the ruling of the Law to attach him to him.
The news regarding the birth of the son of Hasan (peace be upon him) has come from more directions than what establishes lineages in the Law.
And we will mention a portion of that later, if God Almighty wills.

key_terms.إِلْحَاقٌ: Legal attachment of a child to a father
key_terms.صَاحِبُ الزَّمَانِ: Master of the Age (referring to the Mahdi)

ai.seo_question: How did the Imams conceal their lineage and what legal proofs establish their birth?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi contextualizes the concealment of the Imam's lineage within the established social custom of 'kitman' (hiding) to protect the heir from familial greed, a practice he observes frequently in his own time. He validates this through Islamic legal principles where lineage is established via the testimony of two just Muslims or a valid marriage contract, emphasizing that the widespread attestation of the Mahdi's birth exceeds the rigorous standards required for genealogical proof.
